transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I, uh, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. It's probably nothing major, but... I guess I came in because lately, nothing really feels like mine anymore. 

I don't know if I'm explaining that right, so please let me know if I'm not making sense. But I used to get really excited about things, you know? Like checking out murals, going for runs, watching basketball... even just making a really good drink at work. I'm a bartender, and I usually take pride in that. But now I just sort of... stand there. It's like I just don't care about any of it anymore. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing people usually come here for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, let's see... I'd say it's been going on for about two months? Give or take. I hope I'm remembering that right, I definitely don't want to give you the wrong timeline. 

It mostly started right around the time the bar was bought out. The new owners came in and, well, they changed pretty much everything I had been working toward there. Which, you know, is fine! Business is business, and I know I shouldn't let it get to me so much. I should just roll with the punches. But... yeah, I'd say about two months. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you helpful answers.
Have you noticed a decrease in your interest or enjoyment in activities you used to like, such as checking out murals, going for runs, or making drinks at work?

Yes, exactly. I'm sorry, I know I kind of dumped all that on you right when we started talking—I hope I wasn't rambling too much earlier. But yes, that's exactly it. 

The runs, the basketball, making the drinks... I just don't get that spark anymore. I still do my job, of course! I don't want you to think I'm slacking off or letting people down at the bar, I definitely still put in the hours. It's just... internally, I just sort of stand there and feel like I don't care about any of it. 

I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you been feeling like you’re letting people down or that you’re not good at things you used to feel confident about?

Well... I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm throwing a pity party or anything. I know people go through worse. But... yeah, I guess I have been feeling that way a bit. 

When the bar got bought out, I had... I had made some promises. To the younger bartenders, you know, about moving up. And to some local artists about giving them space for their work. And now that's all gone. I just... I keep thinking I really let them down. I feel terrible about it. Like I wrecked their shot at something good, and... I don't know, maybe I deserve whatever happens to me because of it. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds really dramatic. I shouldn't be complaining so much. Does that... is that helpful for you to know? I hope I'm not oversharing.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two months?

Depressed? Well... I don't know if I'd use that word, really. I try my best to keep a positive attitude, you know? I definitely don't want to be walking around bringing everyone else down, especially at the bar. 

So... no, I wouldn't say I feel down most of the day. I mean, I still put on a smile for the customers and get through my shifts just fine. I guess I haven't really noticed it being an all-day kind of thing. Maybe just... I don't know, a little tired or flat sometimes? But definitely not the whole day. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just don't want to make it sound like I'm falling apart or making a big deal out of nothing when I'm really trying to keep it together. Am I making sense?
Have you noticed that you're feeling more tired than usual or that you don't have the energy to do things you normally do, even when you're not physically active or stressed?

Well... I mean, I try not to complain about it too much, you know? I'm fifty-one, so I know I'm not a kid anymore, and being on your feet is just part of the job. I really don't want to sound lazy or like I'm making excuses. 

But... yeah, I guess I have been pretty wiped out lately. It's weird. Like, by the time I carry a couple cases of liquor from the back room, or just set up the well before we open... my body feels like I've already worked a double shift. And that's even if I barely did anything at all that day before coming in. 

I still push through and get the job done, though! I promise I'm not slacking on the clock. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like losing interest in food or losing weight without trying?

Well... I mean, I'm definitely not starving myself or anything on purpose. I know how important it is to keep your strength up, especially working behind a bar. I'd never want to pass out on a shift and cause a scene, you know? 

But... I guess I haven't been eating as much as I probably should. It's just... I get so busy, and most days I honestly just forget to eat. I won't even realize it until my hands start shaking a little while I'm pouring drinks. And then, I don't know, maybe after closing I'll try to grab a few bites of whatever's cold in the back, but... lately, just looking at it makes me feel a little sick to my stomach. 

I'm sure it's just stress from the buyout and everything. I don't want you to think I have an eating problem or anything like that. I'm still trying my best to take care of myself. Does that make sense? I hope that's what you were asking.
Have you felt tired or low on energy nearly every day, even when you haven’t been physically active or stressed?

I think... wait, didn't we just talk about this? I mean, I don't want to repeat myself if you already got what you needed. I'm sorry if I'm getting confused, I just want to make sure I'm following along right. 

But yeah, like I was saying before, I do get pretty wiped out, even when I haven't done much. I really try not to let it show, though. I just push through it. I hope I'm answering your questions the way you need me to? I can try to explain it differently if that wasn't helpful.
Over the past two months, have you found that you don’t get any pleasure or satisfaction out of things you used to enjoy, like making drinks, watching basketball, or going for runs?

Well... I mean, I don't want to sound ungrateful for the things I have. I know I have a good job and a good life, and I really try to keep a positive attitude about everything. I definitely don't want to come across as one of those people who just complains all the time. 

But... yeah, I guess that's actually the main reason I came in to see you. It's just... nothing feels like mine anymore. I used to get so fired up about things, you know? Like checking out new murals around the city, or going for a run, or even just watching a basketball game. I used to really take pride in mixing a great drink for a customer, too. 

Now... I don't know, I just kind of stand there. It's like I don't care about any of it anymore, and I hate feeling that way. I'm really trying to snap out of it, I promise. I just... I don't know how. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right for you.
Have you felt like nothing you do is enjoyable or gives you pleasure, even the things you used to really like?

Oh, um... I'm so sorry, I must not have explained myself very well just a second ago. I know you kind of just asked me about this, so I probably didn't give you a clear enough answer. I definitely don't want to make your job harder or waste your time! 

But yes, that's exactly it. Like I was trying to say before, that's really the main reason I came in to see you. It just feels like... like nothing is mine anymore. I used to get so excited about things, you know? Going for my runs, checking out the new murals downtown, watching basketball, or even just mixing a really good drink for someone at work. And now... I just kind of stand there. It's like I completely lost the ability to care about any of it, even though I'm really trying my best to stay positive. 

I feel terrible even admitting that out loud, because I know I should be more grateful for the things I have. I hope I'm making a little more sense this time? Please let me know if I'm not answering these the right way, I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you felt down or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I feel depressed, exactly. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm whining or anything. I try really hard to keep a smile on my face, especially at work. You kind of have to when you're behind the bar, you know? 

I guess I've just been feeling a little... flat? Or maybe just in a funk lately. But I wouldn't say it's all day, every day for weeks on end. I definitely have moments where I'm okay, or at least I try to be. I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is, because I know people go through much harder things. I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to be honest without sounding like I'm throwing a pity party for myself.
Have you felt like you can’t experience any pleasure at all, even in moments when you’d usually expect to enjoy something, like seeing a good friend or finishing a task you care about?

Oh, gosh... I feel terrible because I know we've kind of been talking about this, and I really hope I'm not frustrating you by repeating myself. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

But, um, yes... that's really the heart of it. Even if I see a buddy or finish a tough shift, it's just... I don't know, it just doesn't register. Like I was saying before, it's why I made the appointment. Nothing feels like mine anymore. I used to get a real kick out of finding a new mural, or getting a good sweat in on a run, or catching a game. Even just pouring a perfect drink for someone—I took pride in that. And now... I just stand there. It's like I'm completely disconnected from it all, and I just can't make myself care, no matter how hard I try to force a smile. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds awful, and I really don't want to sound ungrateful. I'm trying my best to push through it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Over the past two months, have you had a period where you felt this way—like you couldn’t enjoy anything—for two weeks straight without improvement?

Well, um... I really hope I'm not making too big a deal out of this, because I know change is just a part of life, right? You just have to adapt. But, um, yeah... it's been about two months now. 

Basically, it started right around the time the bar got bought out. All the stuff I had been working toward just... got changed overnight by the new owners. I really tried to just roll with the punches and keep a good attitude about it, I promise I did. But ever since then, for these last couple of months straight, it's just been this constant feeling where I can't seem to enjoy anything. 

I feel a little silly letting work stuff get to me this much, I really do. I know I should be stronger than that. Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right timeline for what you need.
Have you felt a loss of pleasure or interest in nearly all activities, including the ones you used to enjoy, for most of the day, more days than not, over the past two months?

Well, um... yeah, I guess I've kind of touched on this a bit already, and I really hope I'm not talking your ear off about it. But yes, that's... that's exactly it. For the last couple of months, mostly every day, it's just been this... this total lack of interest. 

I know I mentioned it before, but it's really the main reason I came in. It's just so frustrating because I used to be such an active guy, you know? I'd get so excited about finding a new mural in the city, or going for a long run, or just watching a basketball game. Even at work, I took real pride in mixing a great drink for someone. And now... I just stand there. It's like none of it belongs to me anymore, and I just can't bring myself to care about any of it. 

I really try to push past it, I swear I do. I don't want to be a downer to the people around me. I just... I don't know why I can't snap out of it. Is it normal to feel this disconnected from everything for this long? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right.

But, um, yes... that's really the heart of it. Even if I see a buddy or finish a tough shift, it's just... I don't know, it just doesn't register. Like I was saying before, it's why I made the appointment. Nothing feels like mine anymore. I used to get a real kick out of finding a new mural, or getting a good sweat in on a run, or catching a game. Even just pouring a perfect drink for someone—I took pride in that. And now... I just stand there. It's like I'm completely disconnected from it all, and I just can't make myself care, no matter how hard I try to force a smile. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds awful, and I really don't want to sound ungrateful. I'm trying my best to push through it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a loss of pleasure or interest in activities for a continuous period of at least two weeks, which would support the diagnosis of a major depressive episode.
doctor.question: Over the past two months, have you had a period where you felt this way—like you couldn’t enjoy anything—for two weeks straight without improvement?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about two months, since the bar was bought out and everything I had been working toward got changed.
target_item.reason: The doctor is explicitly asking about the duration of the symptoms, specifically inquiring if the patient has felt this way for a period of two weeks straight over the past two months.

patient.answer:
Well, um... I really hope I'm not making too big a deal out of this, because I know change is just a part of life, right? You just have to adapt. But, um, yeah... it's been about two months now. 

Basically, it started right around the time the bar got bought out. All the stuff I had been working toward just... got changed overnight by the new owners. I really tried to just roll with the punches and keep a good attitude about it, I promise I did. But ever since then, for these last couple of months straight, it's just been this constant feeling where I can't seem to enjoy anything. 

I feel a little silly letting work stuff get to me this much, I really do. I know I should be stronger than that. Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right timeline for what you need.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a loss of pleasure or interest in activities they previously enjoyed for a significant portion of the day, more days than not, over the past two months, which is a key differentiator between F32.1 (Moderate Depressive Episode) and F33.1 (Recurrent Depressive Disorder, Currently Moderate Episode).
doctor.question: Have you felt a loss of pleasure or interest in nearly all activities, including the ones you used to enjoy, for most of the day, more days than not, over the past two months?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I came in because nothing feels like mine anymore—I used to get excited about murals, runs, basketball, even making a good drink, and now I just stand there like I don't care about any of it.
target_item.reason: The doctor is again asking about the loss of pleasure or interest in nearly all activities over the past two months, which directly matches the Loss_of_Interest symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Well, um... yeah, I guess I've kind of touched on this a bit already, and I really hope I'm not talking your ear off about it. But yes, that's... that's exactly it. For the last couple of months, mostly every day, it's just been this... this total lack of interest. 

I know I mentioned it before, but it's really the main reason I came in. It's just so frustrating because I used to be such an active guy, you know? I'd get so excited about finding a new mural in the city, or going for a long run, or just watching a basketball game. Even at work, I took real pride in mixing a great drink for someone. And now... I just stand there. It's like none of it belongs to me anymore, and I just can't bring myself to care about any of it. 

I really try to push past it, I swear I do. I don't want to be a downer to the people around me. I just... I don't know why I can't snap out of it. Is it normal to feel this disconnected from everything for this long? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right.
